paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning methods for Fourier-based distribution estimation with application in option pricing

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical supervised learning experiment: a PQC is trained to approximate the PDF of the underlying asset price, extract Fourier coefficients via DFT, and price a European vanilla put option under Black-Scholes dynamics.

algorithm.variant: PQC-based supervised learning for PDF approximation with Fourier coefficient extraction
algorithm.ansatz: Layered PQC with data-encoding block Rx(x) and trainable Ry(θ) gates; regular n×n configurations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initialization implied; randomness in initial quantum model weights discussed

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input x is encoded through Rx(x) gates; trainable Ry(θ) gates form the variational block
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize empirical H1 risk for PDF approximation: RS_h1(f*, f) = (1/I) Σ_i (f*(xi)-f(xi))^2 + (1/I) Σ_i (df*/dx(xi)-df/dx(xi))^2

problem_instance.description: Pricing a European vanilla put option with Black-Scholes underlying; PDF of normalized log-price is approximated and Fourier coefficients are used to compute the option price.

dataset_specification.transformation: Xt = log(St/K) with Xt ~ N(log(S0/K) + (r - 0.5σ^2)t, σ^2 t)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Training performed on [-2π, 2π] with data rescaled to [-π, π]; Fourier coefficients of the trained circuit extracted by DFT on direct evaluations in [-π, π]
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 repetitions; convergence assessed versus dataset size and PQC dimension; comparison against exact option price

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Rescale data from [-2π, 2π] to [-π, π]; compute empirical derivatives for differential loss; DFT used to recover Fourier coefficients from trained circuit outputs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert complex exponential Fourier coefficients ck to trigonometric coefficients Af_k and Bf_k; combine with analytically computed payoff coefficients Ck and Dk to price the option

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical self-supervised learning experiment: a PQC is trained to approximate the CDF from unlabeled samples, with derivative-informed loss terms, then Fourier coefficients are extracted to price a European vanilla put option.

algorithm.variant: PQC-based self-supervised learning for CDF approximation with differential loss and Fourier coefficient extraction
algorithm.ansatz: Layered PQC with data-encoding block Rx(x) and trainable Ry(θ) gates; regular n×n configurations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initialization implied; randomness in initial quantum model weights discussed

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input x is encoded through Rx(x) gates; trainable Ry(θ) gates form the variational block
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize combined empirical risk for CDF and PDF: RT_l2,l2(F) = RX_T,l2(F) + RT_l2(f), with boundary constraints at the domain extremes
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Additional boundary penalty terms enforcing CDF behavior at the extremes of the sample domain

problem_instance.description: Pricing a European vanilla put option using only samples from the underlying asset distribution; CDF is learned self-supervisedly and used in a Fourier-based valuation formula.

dataset_specification.transformation: Xt = log(St/K) with Xt ~ N(log(S0/K) + (r - 0.5σ^2)t, σ^2 t)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Unlabeled samples only; empirical CDF used as pseudo-labels; training performed on [-2π, 2π] with data rescaled to [-π, π]; DFT applied to direct circuit evaluations in [-2π, 2π]
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 repetitions; convergence assessed versus dataset size and PQC dimension; comparison against exact option price

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct empirical CDF from samples; compute derivative-based loss terms; rescale data from [-2π, 2π] to [-π, π]; DFT used to recover Fourier coefficients from trained circuit outputs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert complex exponential Fourier coefficients ck to trigonometric coefficients Af_k and Bf_k; combine with analytically computed payoff coefficients Ck and Dk to price the option

experiments.description: Amplitude-estimation benchmark experiment: mRQAE is used to estimate Fourier coefficients of the underlying PDF for option pricing, with shot count varied to study accuracy and cost.

algorithm.variant: modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (mRQAE) benchmark for Fourier coefficient estimation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Precision/tolerance controlled by mRQAE; increasing tolerance used to vary shot count

hyperparameters.shots_per_coefficient: approximately 5000 on average for high accuracy
hyperparameters.total_shots: hundreds of thousands for final price

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distribution of asset paths is encoded into amplitudes of a quantum state; Fourier coefficients of the PDF are estimated via amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Fourier coefficients Af_k and Bf_k of the PDF f(y|x) over [a,b] using mRQAE-based sampling

problem_instance.description: Same European vanilla put option under Black-Scholes dynamics; benchmark against Methods I and II for Fourier coefficient extraction and pricing.
problem_instance.dataset_size: number of circuit executions varied by tolerance; around 5000 shots per coefficient on average
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Exact simulation of asset evolution assumed; coefficients estimated from sampled asset values Si and corresponding f(Si); no numerical SDE discretization needed for Black-Scholes
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Accuracy and variability evaluated as a function of shot count; compared against PQC-based Methods I and II

quantum_resources.num_shots: approximately 5000 shots per coefficient on average; hundreds of thousands total for final price

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Exact simulation of Black-Scholes asset paths; sample-based estimation of Fourier coefficients; tolerance-driven shot allocation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use estimated Fourier coefficients Af_k and Bf_k together with analytically computed payoff coefficients Ck and Dk to compute the option price

speedup_claims.conditions: QAMC / QAE setting for expectation estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the quadratic improvement in mean squared error from QAMC, but does not provide a direct numerical head-to-head benchmark for this experiment.
